Vision, Aims & Values
Kingsdale A Place to Be A Culture of Respect and Inclusivity
Think of a beautiful place where people want to bewhere there is a sense of purpose and possibilityThink of a community enriched by the power of diversityrespecting rights and reflecting responsibilityThink of a place to inspire our creativity and to discoverwho we could or should beThink of a community whose joie de vivre is to helpeach other overcome adversitiesA place to transform and to be transformedA place to cherish and to be cherishedA place to enable and to be enabledProvocative partners we shall be but our raison d’etre is aboutdreams and destiniesDon’t think of you and me. Think of us and we.Unity of purpose is our identityParticipate and be the school we’d all be proud to seeA cultured respected reflective place of studyEveryone empowered to become the best that they can be
Fac Omnia Ad Dei Gloriam
© Kingsdale Foundation School
‘Pupils are rightly very proud of their school. They really enjoy their learning and talk with enthusiasm about the school’s culture of mutual respect and inclusivity.’ - Ofsted 2023.
Our Aims
Kingsdale aims to improve the quality of education and raise levels of attainment through the implementation of a range of innovative strategies, works and practices which will sustain the School as a community centre of learning excellence.
Kingsdale aims to offer an innovative and creative curriculum, which meets the needs of all young people in the 21st Century.
We aim for Kingsdale graduates to be effective independent learners whose success is promoted by personalised curricula and who are able to present themselves well.
We wish to produce adaptable and well-educated young people who have developed their skills and confidence in a strong moral and spiritual culture.
Our Ethos
Kingsdale promotes academic and personal excellence, applauds achievement, cherishes success and celebrates our differences.
Kingsdale is dedicated to the betterment of each and every pupil, producing self-confident, responsible and articulate young people who care for and respect themselves and one another.
The school is proud of and values its pupils, parents and staff and takes pride in the community it serves.
At Kingsdale, we understand that with freedom comes responsibility.
The school manages change in education and in young people.
Kingsdale provides a welcoming environment, which seeks to uplift the spirit, protect the dignity and enlighten those who come into contact with it.

Welcome to Kingsdale
'Leaders aim to nurture the talents of pupils through their scholar programmes in mathematics, music, art and sport.’ - Ofsted 2023
Co-educational Academy of Advanced, Artistic and Academic Studies
‘Students come first at the school and everything possible is done to support them. This is a very high achieving school and competition between students is encouraged and students thrive on it. Students feel safe and secure and they feel valued. They are very keen to learn and to achieve their very best. They show concern for each other and are very supportive of more vulnerable students. The emphasis at Kingsdale is on wellbeing and achievement and the school is fully aware that the two go together and are not separate entities.’
Inclusion Quality Mark & Centre of Excellence Report 2015
‘Everyone at Kingsdale Foundation School should be congratulated for having achieved Gold accreditation as an Investors in People organisation.’
‘There is values-based leadership in evidence and the values are at the heart of the way the organisation operates with all stakeholders...’
‘The positive ethos of Kingsdale is lived day-in, day-out and is focused on the whole person, both for children and staff.’
‘Your commitment to supporting the community is a great example of your values in action…Kingsdale Foundation School has a deep-rooted commitment to community involvement.’
‘All those interviewed agreed that professionalism, learning and coaching, expertise, collaboration, teamwork, innovation and the people culture are what make Kingsdale the success it is today and they are happy working there.’
Investors In People - We Invest in People: Gold Accreditation – March 2023
Kingsdale Foundation School
Kingsdale promotes academic and personal excellence, applauds achievement, cherishes success and celebrates our differences. Kingsdale is one of the most popular schools in the country and caters for the needs of a truly wonderful, talented and diverse community. Kingsdale is particularly well suited to aspirational children, teachers and families.
Kingsdale is proud of its Mathematical, Musical and Sports heritage. We offer scholarships for new entrants to the school who show mathematical, musical or sporting talent. Scholars receive free individual or small group tuition provided by expert professionals, to the value of £1,000 per annum.
Kingsdale is a founding member of Southwark School's Learning Partnership (SSLP) which is a unique collaboration between local maintained and independent schools that includes Dulwich College, James Alleyn's Girls' School and Alleyn's School.
Kingsdale is an independent academy convertor school (mainstream) and is not a part of a chain or sponsored academy arrangement.
We invite you to take a virtual tour or to come and see us in action. We are confident that you will like what you see.

Duke of Edinburgh
Duke of Edinburgh's Award at Kingsdale Foundation School
Kingsdale Foundation School is proud to be associated with this prestigious Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme.
Over the past few years, The Duke of Edinburgh Award scheme has become progressively more popular at Kingsdale. Open to students in Year 9, it provides all with an enjoyable, challenging, and rewarding programme, focusing directly on the student’s personal independent development. Students start at the Bronze Award level in Year 9 and then go on to complete their Silver award in Years 10 to 13. The scheme is unique; the student becomes responsible for their own progression rather a competitive experience. With that in mind each student’s programme is centred on abilities and interests chosen by them.
When students undertake the Duke of Edinburgh Award, they develop transferable skills and attributes that help them become well-rounded individuals and confident young adults. The Award is highly regarded by colleges, universities and employers who value its significance and the range of skills it can develop in young people.
Self-belief & self-confidence.
A sense of identity initiative.
A sense of responsibility.
An awareness of their strengths.
The ability to prioritise and use time effectively alongside their school work.
The ability to learn from and give to others in the community.
Problem solving, presentation and communication skills.
Leadership and teamwork skills.
Students from Year 9 upwards can express an interest in joining the Award, which involves participating in a range of activities including overnight camping excursions and hikes.
For more information about the Duke of Edinburgh Award provision at Kingsdale and how your child can participate in this scheme, please contact Mr Dennington by email at doe@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk
You can also visit the following useful links:What is the Duke of Edinburgh Award Programme?

Communications
Absence or Lateness
Parents are requested to report all student absence as soon as possible on the day of absence.
Arrangements for Absence Reporting
There are several ways to report your child late or absent to school although many parents find email the most efficient. The relevant Pastoral Assistant for your child’s year group as listed below.
year7absence@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk for the Year 7 Pastoral Assistant
year8absence@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk for the Year 8 Pastoral Assistant
year9absence@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk for the Year 9 Pastoral Assistant
year10absence@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk for the Year 10 Pastoral Assistant
year11absence@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk for the Year 11 Pastoral Assistant
Year 12 & 13 Absence
year12&13absence@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk for the Year 12 & 13 Pastoral Assistant
Alternatively, to report your child late or absent by phone, please contact the school on 0208 670 7575 and select Option 2 from the menu. You will then be able to select the required extension number for the relevant Pastoral Assistant for your child’s year group.
Where a student is absent and the School has not been informed, an information text will be sent from the appropriate Pastoral Assistant to the parent advising them of the absence as part of the First Day Contact protocols.
In the interests of encouraging excellent levels of attendance and punctuality, parents are routinely informed of student lateness / absence from the first registration via an automatic email. Please be advised that this communication will also be sent where a parent has informed the school that their child will be late to school. Summaries of student attendance and punctuality can be accessed via www.schoolworkspace.co.uk, which gives an easy overview in form of dials as well as allowing parents to explore attendance in detail. Please contact attendanceoffice@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk should you need support with accessing this.
Parent's Forum
Parents' Forums take place each half term on the third Friday of the month. All forums take place between 5.30 & 7.15pm.
Forums are now 'blended' events, with parents in attendance in the POD/school site and also on MS Teams online. The access code for MS Teams is always included in the Agenda for each meeting, downloadable below. Agendas for each forum are posted in advance and a reminder sent by email and text.
Parents and carers of students at Kingsdale Foundation School can add their name to the Parents’ Forum email list by contacting the school via parentsforum@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk

To assist parents with contacting members of staff at the school, we have produced a comprehensive Communication Directory, detailing the key email addresses by type and query.

Art
Contained within the range of extremely popular and successful subjects comprising the Art, Design and Technology Faculty at Kingsdale, the Art Department is well-established as a powerhouse of creative achievement in Kingsdale.
Aims: The Art Department vision is ‘To enrich the quality of experiences, by providing an experimental, contemporary curriculum, that stimulates, inspires, excites and challenges students, and generates future passionate and ambitious innovators and new thinkers.’
Facilities: Within the Department we have twelve specialist Art teachers and one Art technician. The standard of teaching in the Art Department is outstanding. This has been recognised by Ofsted and throughout the school. The facilities we offer include a specialist ceramics studio with attached kiln room, a specialist photography studio and computer suite with both Mac and PC packages, a darkroom and eight general art studios that are used for painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, graphics and textiles. The Art Department also has its own Art Gallery to display our students’ work. Within the Department we offer four areas of specialism - Fine Art, Textiles, Photography and Graphics.
Sketchbooks:
We also encourage students to use their sketchbook in a range of approaches that include:
recording, exploring and storing visual information.
working out ideas, plans, proposals and designs.
explore possibilities from their own imagination.
analysing methods and techniques.
Galleries and Museums:
We maintain strong links with the Dulwich Picture Gallery, located just a few minutes away from the school. We also visit other London galleries and museums, such as the National Portrait Gallery, the Tate Modern, the Tate Britain, the Saatchi Gallery, the Courtauld Institute, the Wellcome Collection and the Horniman Museum. We also offer an Art & Design trip, usually overseas, to our Key Stage 5 Art, Graphics, Textiles and Photography students. We have previously visited Paris, Berlin, Florence, and Barcelona. Trips prove to be uniquely enriching for students many of whom produce work while away towards their final coursework projects.
INSTAGRAM
Arts Award
We offer Arts Award to Key Stage 3 & 4 students who are interested in the Arts. We currently run the bronze and silver awards in our after-school club. Within the Arts Award, students take part in a range of workshops and activities. They also go on a gallery visit to enhance their appreciation and understanding of Art. Students who achieve the Gold Award will gain 16 UCAS points.

Drama
The Drama department at Kingsdale is student-centered and believe that young people should be treated as artists, as their work builds on great effort, imagination, personal ideas and creative problem solving. We teach students the very highest standards of performance skills to allow their creative ideas to be unleashed at Kingsdale and beyond. We explore our heritage and modernity through a diverse range of plays that encompass the cannon and look beyond Britain to international works as well as those from less well represented groups.
Through opportunities to delve into the cultural and literary history of drama our students can build their knowledge and cultural capital. Drama is used to promote creativity, problem solving, creative leadership, self-discipline, and confidence. Outside of the classroom our students can learn from professional actors, writers and directors to help them understand the opportunities in the arts, empowering them as cultural citizens.

Music
Opened in 2008 by saxophonist Courtney Pine, Kingsdale Foundation School’s Music Department is a place full of energy, enthusiasm, and achievement. Students thrive in Music at Kingsdale and enjoy making music in a fantastic first-class environment.
All pupils in Year 7 and 8 attend weekly Music lessons and from Year 9 they may opt to study GCSE Music through until Year 11. At Key Stage 5, two different A-level courses are offered: Music and Music Technology. In addition to classroom Music lessons, there is a jam-packed extracurricular offer including ensembles of every style available at lunchtimes and after-school.

Careers
‘Leaders have designed a curriculum that is broad and ambitious for all pupils. For example, nearly all pupils study two languages from the start of Year 7.’
Pupils achieve exceptionally well in a wide range of subjects and attain highly at GCSE and A level.’
Kingsdale Foundation School has been recognised for its outstanding careers work. The school has been awarded the national Quality in Careers Standard by Prospects. The national Quality in Careers Standard is awarded to schools and education providers who can demonstrate the importance they place on careers and how they support students to make decisions about their life after school.
Careers Education Information and Guidance has a high profile in school, with the statutory Gatsby Benchmarks underpinning the programme.
Careers Education is integrated in the curriculum. Students are enabled to explore their own career aspirations throughout their life at school and make informed decisions about their future career pathways through a structured programme of curricular and extracurricular activities. The programme aims to encourage students to be ambitious, broaden their horizons and explore their own career aspirations throughout their life at school, enable them to make informed decisions about their future career pathways and ensure their readiness to take the next step in their learning or career. The careers team periodically evaluates the approach and we have the CEIAG development plan in place. The plan takes into account cdi careers audit to determine the learning outcomes.
At Kingsdale, we take very seriously our role and responsibilities in equipping our students for their future careers and the world of work. We engage our community, especially parents, in creating links with employers, employees and the world of work. The school is situated in South London with easy access to a range of occupations e.g. finance, law, performing arts and others. The school works with Southwark EBA to ensure students have access to work experience opportunities. This year, due to the pandemic, the school has explored and offered several virtual platforms to provide CEIAG services to students successfully.
Kingsdale is committed to Quality in Careers Standards Award.

Academic Information
Academic Reports & Assessment
Assessment, Recording & Reporting Overview
Student attainment and progress data, along with attendance and behaviour information, is shared with parents & carers securely through our online portal called Go4Schools. This service can be accessed via www.go4schools.com using the contact information provided to the school at enrolment. Please use the link at the bottom of this page for further details on how to login to this service.
A full schedule for parents for academic assessment and reporting key dates can be downloaded at the bottom of this page.
Please email askict@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk should you require assistance with logging into Go4Schools
Full Academic Reports and Parents' Evenings (Teacher comments and latest attainment data)
Students receive one Full Academic Report per academic year, which is usually preceded by their formal examination week. The Full Report is issued one week before the scheduled Parents’ Evening. The Full Report contains detailed summaries from all of a child’s teachers on their areas of progress and development. Full Reports are issued online via our parent portal www.go4schools.com
The dates for the issuing of the Full Report, along with the Parents’ Evening for each year group are listed below. Parent's Evenings are held annually for each year group and are online events via our video-conferencing software. Parents can book 5 minute online discussions with each of their child's teachers. Appointments for parents’ evenings are made online from the Thursday before a Parents’ Evening via www.kingsdalefoundation.parentseveningsystem.co.uk
More information on these important systems can be located on our school website here.
Short Academic Reports (Latest attainment & effort data only - no comments)
Short Reports Cycle
In addition to one Full Academic Report per year, students all receive a number of Short Academic Reports. These reports are smaller than the full report and contain a summary of key academic information for parents to use to consider their child’s progress.
Short Reports are usually issued termly from the second Autumn Half Term, although not in a term where a student has received their Full Report or undertaken an examination series and received an Examination Report (please see schedule below).
In the first Autumn Half Term, Year 7 students will receive a ‘Snapshot Report’ which will contain a one line comment from staff, alongside an effort and organisation grade.
Technical support and hard copies of the Short Reports can be obtained from Ms Otubu on 02086559727 or via email attendanceoffice@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk

Libraries & Literacy
‘Leaders aim to nurture the talents of pupils through their scholar programmes in mathematics, music, art and sport.’‘’Leaders have designed a curriculum that is broad and ambitious for all pupils. For example, nearly all pupils study two languages from the start of Year 7. -Ofsted 2023
At Kingsdale Foundation School, we believe that strong literacy is fundamental to students’ success across the curriculum and beyond school. Reading, writing, vocabulary and spoken language are therefore a whole-school priority, with all subject areas playing an important role in developing confident, articulate and independent learners.
Our Libraries
Our Lower School Library, for Key Stage 3, and Upper School Library, for Key Stages 4 and 5, are central to the academic and cultural life of the school. They provide welcoming spaces in which students can read for pleasure, undertake independent study, complete homework and access a wide range of curriculum and reference materials.
Students are introduced to the library facilities when they join Kingsdale and are encouraged to make regular use of them throughout their time at the school.
Our library provision includes a broad range of fiction, non-fiction and reference materials, alongside digital resources, newspapers and multilingual texts. We are committed to ensuring that reading is accessible to all students, including those with SEND and students who require adapted or carefully selected reading materials.
The libraries also support subject-specific learning and independent study, enabling students to extend their knowledge beyond the classroom and develop the research and information literacy skills they will need for further study and adult life.
Developing a Culture of Reading
Reading for pleasure has a high profile at Kingsdale. We want students not only to become proficient readers but also to discover books, writers and subjects that interest, challenge and inspire them.
Kingsdale has a long history of promoting reading across the school. Our involvement as a Reading Connects school helped to establish the principle that developing a reading culture is a whole-school responsibility, with the libraries at the heart of this work.
The school has also participated in the Southwark Book Award, connecting our students with other primary and secondary schools and with library services across Southwark.
This commitment continues through our celebration of the National Year of Reading, providing an additional opportunity to place reading at the centre of school life. Throughout the year, we will continue to celebrate books and reading through activities, recommendations, competitions, assemblies and special events, encouraging students and families to make reading part of everyday life.
Our libraries regularly support author visits, workshops and literary events, giving students opportunities to encounter established and emerging writers and to engage with literature beyond their normal classroom experience. Details of forthcoming events and reading initiatives are shared through our website and Parental News.
Literacy Across the Curriculum
At Kingsdale, literacy is not confined to English lessons. All teachers have a responsibility for supporting students to read, write, speak and use subject-specific vocabulary successfully within their disciplines.
Our whole-school approach places particular emphasis on:
developing ambitious vocabulary and subject-specific language;
developing students’ speaking, listening and oracy;
promoting accurate, purposeful and effective written communication;
Bedrock Literacy: Years 7 and 8
Students in Years 7 and 8 use Bedrock Literacy as part of our structured approach to developing vocabulary, reading comprehension and wider literacy skills.
Bedrock provides students with regular opportunities to encounter ambitious vocabulary and challenging texts while developing their understanding of language in context. Students’ engagement and progress are monitored so that we can identify where additional support or challenge may be required.
This work complements the literacy teaching taking place across students’ curriculum subjects and supports the development of increasingly confident and independent readers.
Year 9 Literacy
All students in Year 9 have a dedicated literacy lesson once each week.
These lessons build on the foundations established during Years 7 and 8 and help students develop the more sophisticated reading, vocabulary, writing and communication skills they will need as they move towards Key Stage 4.
Year 9 literacy provides an important bridge between our Key Stage 3 literacy provision and the increasingly demanding reading and writing students encounter across their GCSE subjects.
Identifying and Supporting Reading Needs
We use reading-age and other relevant assessment information alongside teacher knowledge to identify students who may require additional literacy support.
Where a need is identified, students may receive targeted support designed to address their particular barriers to reading and literacy. Progress is monitored so that provision can be reviewed and adapted appropriately.
Our aim is to ensure that difficulties with literacy do not prevent any student from accessing the wider curriculum or participating fully in school life.
Reading Beyond the Classroom
Students are encouraged to read widely and regularly, both in school and at home. Reading is promoted through form time, the school libraries, curriculum reading, reading recommendations, competitions and whole-school events.
We also celebrate national events such as World Book Day and National Poetry Day, alongside our wider National Year of Reading programme.
Parents and carers have an important role to play in developing positive reading habits. Our Literacy Hub for Parents and Carers provides practical advice on supporting reading, writing, vocabulary, speaking and listening at home, together with recommended reading and useful strategies.
Library Access
Both libraries are available to students during the school day, including at lunchtime, for reading, homework and independent study.
The Upper School Library and Lower School library is also open after school each weekday until 5.30pm, providing students with additional access to a quiet and well-resourced environment for reading, homework and independent study.

Homework
Homework Timetables
At Kingsdale Foundation School, homework is set regularly in line with our published homework timetables. The homework timetables show the last day each when homework for a particular subject should have been set by the class teacher. Please be advised that subjects that are taught for one lesson a week, such as PSHE/Citizenship or Religious Education, will usually set homework on alternate weeks to allow sufficient time for completion and marking.
The latest Homework Timetables can be downloaded via the link at the bottom of this page.
Online Homework Portal - Satchel One (Show My Homework)
To ensure parents are able to effectively support their children with homework completion, all tasks set by class teachers are recorded on our online portal provided by Satchel One - www.satchelone.com
Using this system, parents are able to log in to view the individualised homework set for each class timetabled for their child. Letters are sent to parents at the start of the academic year detailing how they can access the personalised homework timetable for their children.
The login page for students/parents can be accessed via the website www.showmyhomework.co.uk Technical and logging in support, including retrieval of logging in details, is available by via email homework@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk or by calling 0208 655 9727.
School Homework Expectations
Students are expected to take care and pride over their homework tasks. All homework completed must be headed by a clearly underlined titled, a date and the code H/W to signify that this is a homework task. Homework completed on paper should be neatly secured into the student exercise book or folder as soon as possible. Loose sheets should not be stored in student exercise books or folders.
While all homework tasks are available via the ShowMyHomework online portal, they are encouraged to record all homework tasks set in lessons in their personal school journal. This is to ensure students develop skills as self organisation.
Homework Queries
All homework queries can be directed to our dedicated homework email address at homework@kingsdale.southwark.sch.uk This email can be used to clarify particular homework tasks or to advise staff of particular circumstances or issues pertaining to subject homework. Please ensure that the name of the teacher who set the homework, along with the student's name, are clearly included in the subject line of the email query.

Art
Contained within the range of extremely popular and successful subjects comprising the Art, Design and Technology Faculty at Kingsdale, the Art Department is well-established as a powerhouse of creative achievement in Kingsdale.
Aims: The Art Department vision is ‘To enrich the quality of experiences, by providing an experimental, contemporary curriculum, that stimulates, inspires, excites and challenges students, and generates future passionate and ambitious innovators and new thinkers.’
Facilities: Within the Department we have twelve specialist Art teachers and one Art technician. The standard of teaching in the Art Department is outstanding. This has been recognised by Ofsted and throughout the school. The facilities we offer include a specialist ceramics studio with attached kiln room, a specialist photography studio and computer suite with both Mac and PC packages, a darkroom and eight general art studios that are used for painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, graphics and textiles. The Art Department also has its own Art Gallery to display our students’ work. Within the Department we offer four areas of specialism - Fine Art, Textiles, Photography and Graphics.
Sketchbooks:
We also encourage students to use their sketchbook in a range of approaches that include:
recording, exploring and storing visual information.
working out ideas, plans, proposals and designs.
explore possibilities from their own imagination.
analysing methods and techniques.
Galleries and Museums:
We maintain strong links with the Dulwich Picture Gallery, located just a few minutes away from the school. We also visit other London galleries and museums, such as the National Portrait Gallery, the Tate Modern, the Tate Britain, the Saatchi Gallery, the Courtauld Institute, the Wellcome Collection and the Horniman Museum. We also offer an Art & Design trip, usually overseas, to our Key Stage 5 Art, Graphics, Textiles and Photography students. We have previously visited Paris, Berlin, Florence, and Barcelona. Trips prove to be uniquely enriching for students many of whom produce work while away towards their final coursework projects.
INSTAGRAM
Arts Award
We offer Arts Award to Key Stage 3 & 4 students who are interested in the Arts. We currently run the bronze and silver awards in our after-school club. Within the Arts Award, students take part in a range of workshops and activities. They also go on a gallery visit to enhance their appreciation and understanding of Art. Students who achieve the Gold Award will gain 16 UCAS points.
